name: Shallot
grown_as: The shallot, grown from single bulbs (sets) each of which divides into a cluster of 4 to 12 bulbs. Drawn as a coppery-red-brown shallot such as 'Red Sun' or 'Longor'; others are golden ('Golden Gourmet'), grey or long ('Échalion'). ⚠️ CHECK: William's variety. Not drawn in flower: shallots seldom flower.
habit: A clump of many upright hollow leaves 25 to 40 cm, from a cluster of bulbs joined at a common base at the soil surface.

leaf.arrangement: In two ranks from the neck of each bulb, many bulbs together making a clump
leaf.outline: Long, narrow, hollow, round to half-round tube, 20 to 40 cm by 0.5 to 1 cm, thinner than onion
leaf.base: A sheath wrapping the neck of its bulb

fruit: Not drawn: shallots rarely flower; when they do it is a small round greenish-white head like an onion's.
winter: Bulbs are lifted and dried in summer and stored. Sets planted in winter or early spring show a few thin leaves.

leaf: a long thin hollow round tube, not flat
set: one bulb, teardrop-shaped, taller than wide, with coppery-brown papery skin
a pointed neck and a flat root plate
young: several leaves from one bulb, the bulb already starting to split into two or three
crop: a cluster of several teardrop-shaped coppery bulbs joined at one base, half on top of the soil

look_alikes: Onion grows into one round bulb, not a cluster. Garlic makes a bulb of cloves under one shared skin, with flat leaves. Potato onions (multiplier onions) are the same group and look much the same.
